workPackageTitle: Planar math, primitives, inclusive overlap, swept queries, terrain collision
notes: Entries are added before implementation and are never renumbered (docs/technical/91-verification-strategy.md § Verification registry). This file was created in the same commit that first implements against it, and every entry below was authored before the production code it names.

'status' takes exactly one of 'registered', 'implemented', 'retired' (doc 91 § Entry status). 'evidenceKinds' is read against 'status' (doc 91 § What evidenceKinds means): for a 'registered' entry the list is evidence the verification will produce once built, and nothing may treat it as produced.
The structural validator for this file is owned by TASK-FND-009-002. Until it lands, the shape here matches tests/verification/SIM-007.json exactly.

This file is deliberately NOT named SIM-0*.json. tests/MechaMiner.Simulation.Tests/Support/NegativeControlCoverageTests.cs globs 'SIM-0*.json' and asserts a totals line accounting for every entry across those seven files, so adding an entry to one of them from another work package would break an unrelated package's gate.

This slice implements the planar primitives that player movement needs and nothing else. Swept circle-against-polygon queries, the uniform spatial hash, and terrain collision are the rest of GEO-001's payload; they have no entry here yet because doc 91 forbids renumbering, so they will be appended as VER-GEO-001-005 onward by the task that lands them rather than inserted among these.

Angles are radians measured counterclockwise from simulation east, which is the ordinary atan2(y, x) convention. doc 20 § Numeric and unit conventions puts degrees clockwise from north 'only at display/content boundaries', so the internal representation is deliberately not the player-facing bearing and the conversion is presentation's.

The swept-segment primitive was added by the threat-and-extraction slice, which needed it: a point test on a Pulse Repeater projectile both tunnels at 0.267 m per tick against a 0.44 m body and leaves the muzzle unreachable, so a pursuer standing on the mech - which docs/31:26 permits, since enemies are non-solid - would have been permanently invulnerable to the mech's own weapon. doc 10 § Entity and scene boundary already names swept-area tests as part of this component's job.

entries.summary: The planar vector is a value in gameplay meters with exact arithmetic, magnitude, and squared magnitude, and it refuses a non-finite component at construction rather than propagating NaN into authoritative state.
Normalizing a nonzero vector yields unit magnitude and preserves direction; normalizing the zero vector is an explicit zero direction rather than an arbitrary axis.

Circle-point containment and circle-circle overlap are inclusive and computed from squared distance: a point exactly on the boundary is contained, and two circles at exactly their summed radii overlap.
A direction's bearing round-trips: the bearing of a unit vector reconstructs that vector, and simulation east is exactly zero radians.

Circle-segment overlap is inclusive and computed from squared distances: a segment that only touches the circle overlaps it, a segment whose nearest point is beyond either endpoint is measured to that endpoint rather than to the infinite line, and a degenerate zero-length segment reduces to point containment.
